setup.evaluation: scaffold folds; importance measured on test molecules only
setup.importance_meaning: increase in RMSE when one column is shuffled

hypotheses.statement: The model relies on very few columns
hypotheses.rule: top-2 columns hold at least 50% of the total importance
hypotheses.numbers: top-1 42%, top-2 73%, top-10 80%; top column d_MolLogP 0.452 (fold SD not saved)

hypotheses.rule: at least 50% of columns have importance <= 0

hypotheses.statement: The most important columns are mainly descriptors, not fingerprint bits
hypotheses.rule: at least 6 of the top-10 columns are descriptors
hypotheses.numbers: 9 of the top-10 are descriptors, 1 are fingerprint bits

hypotheses.statement: Near-copies were hiding some importance of the top columns
hypotheses.rule: a top column has near-copies and its importance rises when they are collapsed
hypotheses.numbers: d_MolLogP: 1 near-copies, 0.452 alone -> 0.443 collapsed; d_fr_COO: 2 near-copies, 0.322 alone -> 0.324 collapsed

hypotheses.statement: The top columns stay on top after grouping
hypotheses.rule: the top-2 columns (or their representatives) are still the top-2

limits: Importance shows what the model uses, not what causes the target.
Correlated columns share credit, so a single column's number understates it.
H3 counts the top-10 columns; it does not compare the whole descriptor and fingerprint blocks (that comparison is the cross-validation ablation).
One seed and five scaffold folds; spread over folds is reported, spread over seeds is not.
Verdict rules (such as 50% or 6 of 10) were fixed by the author in advance and are not statistical tests.
